Thessaloniki Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Thessaloniki, Greece

Demolished. Thessaloniki was home to one of the most significant Jewish communities in the world for over two millennia — Jewish settlement here is documented from around 140 BCE, and after waves of Sephardic immigration following the 1492 expulsion from Spain, the city became the largest Jewish community in Greece and a major center of Torah scholarship, with Jews making up a majority of the population by the 1520s. The community endured cycles of growth and devastation — including a catastrophic 1917 fire that destroyed 34 of 37 synagogues — and numbered roughly 50,000 by the eve of WWII, when 48,533 people were deported to the death camps, effectively ending what had been known as a great center of Sephardic Jewry. The cemetery itself, presumed established in the 14th or 15th century, was entirely destroyed and its site is now a university campus; only about 400 Jews returned to Thessaloniki after the war, rebuilding a community that remains Greece's second largest, after Athens.
